newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - Ifo W. German climate index 97.4.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Ifo W. German climate index 97.4.

text.p: Following are reactions to the Ifo institute survey's that the West German Business climate index was 97.4 in October compared with 95.7 in September.

ANN KATRIN JAENKE, COMMERZBANK, FRANKFURT: "The hopes for further rate cuts will fade away. They should end. The bond markets are not in a very good mood about the German economy. "We did not expect as good a result as we saw. This confirms that the economic cycle is going up."

GUENTER REDEKER, CHASE MANHATTAN, LONDON: "I am a bit surprised by the strength of this number. Hopes for a further rate cut (right now) will fade away. Our forecast is looking for a rate cut in the March to April period next year. Until then, the Bundesbank is on hold. They have to have some experience with this historically-low interest rate period.
"Two things must be considered. One is that the German labour market is very weak. The second is that we have not seen the impact of the tight budgets, which come in January."

WOLFGANG BARTH, BAYERISCHE VEREINSBANK, MUNICH: "The Bundesbank is in a very comfortable situation. There is no reason why interest rates should go up now. We still may see a reduction in the repo rate but not shortly. It will depend on the further developments in the economy. The Bundesbank may have a chance to lower rates but not right now."

BRIAN CLAPP, STONE & McCARTHY, LONDON: "It is clearly on the strong side. The three-month moving average has climbed to 3.9 percent from 3.5 percent the month before. It shows the trend is picking up. The recovery seems to be taking root."
